title: The Broken Salt
premise: Noor Winterbourne, a cartographer who once mapped the living borders between realms, has hidden in Saltmere, a city that outlawed magic after the Sundering broke the old covenant. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue and bearing a shard of the broken covenant-stone, Noor is forced to choose between the safe anonymity they built and the inheritance of duty they fled. Pursued by the Wardens' inquisitor and betrayed by an old friend who believes sealing the realms forever is mercy, Noor journeys to the frozen Threshold where the covenant was first sworn. In the end, Noor reforges the covenant not with power but by surrendering their own claim to it — passing the bond to the child, who becomes the first bridge-keeper of a new age — while the long winter breaks over a city learning to unmake its fear.
about_author: Astrid Okonkwo is a former marine cartographer turned novelist who grew up between Lagos and Reykjavik, a childhood she credits for her obsession with borders, tides, and the stories nations tell about their edges. She writes fantasy about people caught between loyalties, and she still keeps an unlabeled map on her study wall that she refuses to explain.

chapters.title: The City That Forbade Wonder
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet Noor selling harmless charms in Saltmere's night market, mapping forbidden doorways from memory, hiding a past as a realm-cartographer. When Warden patrols burn a neighbor's stall, Noor's careful neutrality curdles into quiet shame. Emotional beat: the loneliness of self-erasure — belonging purchased at the price of truth.

chapters.title: A Knock in the First Tongue
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A mud-splattered child appears at Noor's door speaking a language older than any kingdom, clutching a shard of pale stone that hums against Noor's old cartographer's compass. The words translate themselves in Noor's mind: 'The winter is falling. Find the oathkeeper.' Emotional beat: dread and reluctant recognition — the past has found them.

chapters.title: What the Compass Remembers
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with a flashback chapter from three years earlier. The shard matches the missing piece of the covenant-stone Noor helped shatter during the Sundering's last desperate night. Flashback reveals Noor's mentor, Ilsa Vane, ordered the breaking — and that Noor ran rather than choose a side. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; loyalty to a dead mentor vs. truth.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Kind Offer
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Marrow's POV. Marrow interrogates market witnesses, revealing he knows exactly what Noor was. He offers clemency for the child in exchange for the shard, framing the Warden regime as protectors keeping realms apart to prevent another Sundering. His sincerity makes him dangerous. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist; order vs. freedom.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor flees Saltmere with the child, Tess, guided by an old map drawn in blood-ink. They shelter with the Tidebound, a smuggler community still practicing small magics. There Noor learns the long winter isn't weather — it's the dying covenant draining warmth across all realms. Emotional beat: tentative belonging among outcasts.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Lantern
chapters.summary: Tess's POV, rendered through her drawings and fragments of First Tongue. Noor's old friend Bram Oduya — believed dead — appears leading a Warden column; he betrayed the Tidebound's location, believing a sealed covenant will end magic's wars forever. Tess watches Noor waver. Emotional beat: betrayal cuts deepest when the betrayer loves you.

chapters.title: Crossing the White Meridian
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A brutal crossing of the frozen Threshold wastes, where unmapped space rearranges itself around travelers' fears. Noor must use the full depth of their cartographic gift — and accept that mapping means claiming responsibility for what's mapped. Tess begins speaking aloud again. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Grave Has No Stone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the ruined oath-hall, Noor finds Ilsa Vane alive, half-frozen, sustained by the covenant's death throes. Ilsa confesses she broke the stone to stop a war of gods, and begs Noor to let the realms die apart rather than risk reunion. Marrow and Bram arrive. Emotional beat: the mentor's truth reframes everything; no clean villains.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax at the Threshold as the final cold falls. Noor attempts to reforge the covenant alone and fails — the stone demands a willing heir, not a penitent survivor. Choosing trust over control, Noor names Tess bridge-keeper; the child's voice joins the shards into a new covenant. Marrow stands down, undone by witnessing it; Bram turns his lantern against the Wardens' reinforcements. Emotional beat: surrender as strength.

chapters.title: Maps With Edges Again
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue one year later. Spring returns to Saltmere; magic is legal but regulated by the new bridge-order Tess leads. Noor, no longer hiding, opens a school of cartography where students map the reopened doors. Marrow sends a grudging letter of thanks; Bram tends the Tidebound's rebuilt harbor. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance transformed into gift.
